?
In plain words

Before a transaction is final it waits in the mempool, a shared waiting room. Miners pick the transactions paying the highest fee per unit of space (sat/vB) first, roughly one block every ten minutes. Pay more to jump the queue, or pay less and wait.

?
In plain words

Miners race to find the next block by making trillions of guesses per second. Hashrate is how many guesses the whole network makes. Every 2,016 blocks (about two weeks) the difficulty resets so blocks keep arriving about every ten minutes, no matter how much hardware joins or leaves.

?
In plain words

New bitcoin only enter circulation as the reward for mining a block. That reward is cut in half every 210,000 blocks (about four years). This halving means the supply approaches, but never exceeds, 21 million coins, with the last fraction mined around the year 2140.

?
In plain words

Lightning is a network of payment channels built on top of Bitcoin. Two people lock some bitcoin in a channel once, then can pay each other (or anyone connected through other channels) instantly and for fractions of a cent. Only the opening and closing touch the main chain.

UNDER THE HOOD

Data & methodology

Price history & live quote

Loading source dates…

Historical daily USD prices come from Coin Metrics Community Data through May 23, 2026 (when its free price series stopped), then Coinbase Exchange daily closes (UTC). A scheduled job appends each completed day to data.json and refreshes CPI; if it ever falls behind, the page fills the gap from Coinbase on load, so the chart is always current. Circulating supply is computed from the latest block height. The spot quote and recent OHLC candles are fetched from Coinbase Exchange (with Coinbase retail spot as a quote fallback) on load, every minute, and on refresh. If the request fails, the last stored quote or historical observation is shown with its timestamp. The spot chart refreshes recent exchange candles separately from the long-term history. Saved candles are clearly timestamped if the live endpoint is unavailable. A live quote does not extend the long-term historical chart.

Power law

We fit log₁₀(price) = intercept + exponent × log₁₀(days since January 3, 2009) to every positive daily observation. R² is measured in log space. The default historical envelope uses a power law fitted to record-setting local peaks (highest daily price within 365 observations on either side), shifted upward just enough to enclose every loaded daily price, with a small 0.005-log-unit margin. The lower curve uses the fitted trend shifted down to the lowest historical residual, with the same margin. The bounds are calibrated using the full history, not an out-of-sample prediction. Optional ±1σ and ±2σ bands use log-price residual standard deviations and may exclude extreme peaks. No band is a forecast confidence interval. The horizon slider extrapolates this same fit.

Inflation adjustment

U.S. CPI-U, all items, not seasonally adjusted (BLS series CUUR0000SA0). Each daily price is multiplied by the latest CPI value ÷ its month’s CPI. Beyond the latest CPI release, the latest available value is held constant.

View the BLS source ↗

Network data

Mempool, fee estimates, projected and recent blocks, difficulty, hashrate, mining pools, rewards, Lightning statistics and multi-currency prices come from the public mempool.space REST API. Fast-moving data refreshes every minute; hashrate, pools and Lightning every 15 minutes. If a request fails, the last good value or a timestamped saved snapshot (network-snapshot.json) is shown and labelled. Fee costs use typical native SegWit sizes (simple payment ≈ 141 vB). Queue-position estimates assume no new higher-fee transactions arrive. Circulating supply is computed exactly from the current block height and the issuance schedule; it does not subtract coins that are lost or provably unspendable. Future halving dates use the current epoch’s average block time (clamped to 8–12 minutes).

Drawdown

Daily price ÷ the highest price observed up to that date − 1. This uses daily observations, so intraday highs and lows can differ.
